statements.status_notes: GHSA-mx64-mj3q-7prj (GO-2026-5048): the Avro map decoders in github.com/hamba/avro/v2 and in its maintained fork github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 (mapDecoder.Decode and mapDecoderUnmarshaler.Decode in codec_map.go) take each map block's element count from the input and grow the map with no upper bound, so crafted Avro data can exhaust the process's memory. hamba/avro/v2 is archived and every version up to its last release, v2.31.0, is affected with no fix. The fork's v2.33.0 adds a Config.MaxMapAllocSize limit with commit https://github.com/iskorotkov/avro/commit/5192df96a158999344ac96ebcb1f7461d626f6d7, but the limit is zero, meaning unlimited, by default, and the advisory says that upgrading to v2.33.0 alone does not mitigate the issue: a program is protected only when it sets MaxMapAllocSize to a non-zero value: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mx64-mj3q-7prj, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5048 . The Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository lists 24 opentelemetry-collector-contrib-dev builds as of 27 November 2026, 0.156.0-r0 to the current 0.166.0-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64 (48 packages). For each of the 48 Alpine 3.23 packages we checked the control section against its index checksum and read the data archive up to and including the Go build information of /usr/bin/otelcol-contrib, which covers the program's function table (pclntab) and read-only data but not the debug sections at the end of the file. Each program is a Go program for Linux (an ELF executable whose Go build information records GOOS=linux) built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (the Go release and module versions) and the function names in its function table; runtime.main is present in every build as a control. Every build links the vulnerable decoder under the github.com/hamba/avro/v2 import path, including (*mapDecoder).Decode and (*mapDecoderUnmarshaler).Decode. Up to 0.157.0-r0 the build information lists github.com/hamba/avro/v2 v2.31.0 with no replace directive for it, the unfixed release. From 0.158.0-r0 on it lists github.com/hamba/avro/v2 v2.31.0 followed by => github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 v2.33.0, so the code under that import path is the fork release that has the MaxMapAllocSize setting, but with the limit off unless a caller sets it; those builds also list github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 v2.33.1 as a module, but the only functions linked under that import path are 8 to 9 from its pkg/crc64 checksum package, such as github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2/pkg/crc64.Sum, on both architectures in every build from 0.158.0 on; no decoder function under that import path is linked. One caller in these programs is github.com/apache/pulsar-client-go, which the Pulsar receiver and exporter use: its AvroSchema methods are linked in every build, and its AvroSchema.Decode in pulsar/schema.go calls avro.Unmarshal with the package default configuration, which sets no MaxMapAllocSize; the Pulsar receiver itself decodes message payloads with its own trace, metric and log unmarshalers. Pending: a call-path analysis of every caller of the Avro decoders in these programs, to establish whether any of them decodes Avro maps from untrusted input without a MaxMapAllocSize limit.

GHSA-mx64-mj3q-7prj (GO-2026-5048): the Avro map decoders in github.com/hamba/avro/v2 and in its maintained fork github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 (mapDecoder.Decode and mapDecoderUnmarshaler.Decode in codec_map.go) take each map block's element count from the input and grow the map with no upper bound, so crafted Avro data can exhaust the process's memory. hamba/avro/v2 is archived and every version up to its last release, v2.31.0, is affected with no fix. The fork's v2.33.0 adds a Config.MaxMapAllocSize limit with commit https://github.com/iskorotkov/avro/commit/5192df96a158999344ac96ebcb1f7461d626f6d7, but the limit is zero, meaning unlimited, by default, and the advisory says that upgrading to v2.33.0 alone does not mitigate the issue: a program is protected only when it sets MaxMapAllocSize to a non-zero value: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mx64-mj3q-7prj, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5048 . The opentelemetry-collector-contrib-fips-dev packages for Alpine 3.23 are not in the public DHI Alpine repository index; they are published only in the DHI Alpine security repository, which requires authentication and could not be read for this review, so no build of this owner was inspected. Pending: an inspection of every published opentelemetry-collector-contrib-fips-dev build on both architectures, to establish which Avro module, if any, each one links and whether any caller in it sets MaxMapAllocSize. In the non-FIPS opentelemetry-collector-contrib-dev packages, which we did inspect, every build links the Avro map decoder under the github.com/hamba/avro/v2 import path: the unfixed hamba/avro/v2 v2.31.0 in 0.156.0 and 0.157.0, and from 0.158.0 the fork github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 v2.33.0 put in its place by a replace directive, whose limit is off unless a caller sets it. That is not evidence for the FIPS builds, which are built separately.

For each we read the control archive, whose file list names only /usr/bin/otelcol, and the start of the data archive: the Go build ID of /usr/bin/otelcol, which ends in a hash of the program's content, equals the one in the opentelemetry-collector package for Alpine 3.23 of the same build and architecture (0.156.0-0 and 0.156.0-r0, and so on to 0.166.0-1 and 0.166.0-r1), so each Debian build ships the same program as the Alpine build we read. For each of the 48 Alpine 3.23 packages we checked the control section against its index checksum and read the data archive up to and including the Go build information of /usr/bin/otelcol, which covers the program's function table (pclntab) and read-only data but not the debug sections at the end of the file. Each program is a Go program for Linux (an ELF executable whose Go build information records GOOS=linux) built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (the Go release and module versions) and the function names in its function table; runtime.main is present in every build as a control. The opentelemetry-collector-dev binary packages, which the DHI Debian repository lists with Source opentelemetry-collector, are built from the same source with the same versions and are assessed as their own owner, with the same result. No build lists github.com/hamba/avro/v2 or github.com/iskorotkov/avro/v2 in its Go build information, no build has a function under either import path, and the bytes github.com/hamba/avro/v2 appear nowhere in the part of any program we read. The same search finds 559 to 620 functions under github.com/hamba/avro/v2, including (*mapDecoder).Decode, in every opentelemetry-collector-contrib build. The vulnerable Avro decoder is not part of this package.
